{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of agreement (concordance rates, sensitivity, specificity, predictability) between animal model results (in vivo QTc interval prolongation in dogs and monkeys, APD in dogs, rabbits, guinea pigs, sheep) and human clinical outcomes (QTc interval prolongation). It analyzes a large dataset of drugs and provides specific percentages for concordance.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study evaluates the prediction of drug-induced QTc prolongation in humans using nonclinical assays, which falls under safety pharmacology.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on drug-induced ventricular arrhythmia, Torsades de Pointes, and QT interval prolongation, all of which are cardiovascular endpoints.",
  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes a joint HESI/FDA database of nonclinical and clinical QT data from 150 drugs submitted in INDs or NDAs, fitting the definition of a regulatory dataset.",
  "species": [
    "dog",
    "rabbit",
    "guinea-pig",
    "sheep",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The text explicitly mentions 'nonrodent animal studies', 'dogs', 'monkeys', 'rabbit', 'guinea pig', and 'sheep' in the context of the assays evaluated.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study evaluates both the prediction of clinical QT interval prolongation (a hard endpoint) and uses various nonclinical assays (hERG, APD, in vivo QTc) which can be considered secondary biomarkers for predicting this outcome."
}
